title: Congressional Stock Trading Research & Backtests | Signal Congress
excerpt: # Congressional Stock Trading — The Data We analyzed 30,799 congressional stock trades filed under the STOCK Act from 2018–2026. Buying every congressional trade indiscriminately underperforms the S&P 500 by 1.41% at 180 days — Congress, in aggregate, is not a better stock picker than the index. But filtered for bipartisan clusters with committee relevance, the same dataset produces +7.88% alpha at 180 days. The ~9-point spread between the baseline and the signal is what Signal Congress finds. Read our full methodology and statistical caveats → CORE FINDING +7.88% Average 180-day outperformance vs. S&P 500 for cross-chamber bipartisan cluster trades (n=311, 2023–2026) 56.3% Win Rate +7.88% vs SPX Avg Alpha 311 signals Trade Count 2023–2026 Test Period STRATEGY COMPARISON ## Four Strategies, Backtested Starting from all 30,799 congressional trades, we applied progressively tighter filters. The unfiltered baseline loses to the market. The right filter finds significant alpha. Each strategy below is independent — not a funnel. BASELINE (NO FILTER) All congressional purchases vs SPY -1.41% at 180 days · n = 6,325 purchases STRATEGY TRADES WIN RATE ALPHA vs SPX Cross-Chamber Bipartisan Buys ★ 311 56.3% +7.88% High Conviction Sells 57 64.8% +7.20% High Conviction Purchases 181 52.5% +2.52% Large Positions (≥$50K mid) 320 51.5% +2.17% Bipartisan Cluster Buys 760 48.7% +2.14% Low Lag — Fast Disclosure (≤7 days) 452 50.4% +2.13% Senate Purchases (All) 1,015 41.4% -0.12% All Purchases (Baseline) 6,325 43.0% -1.41% House Purchases (All) 5,310 43.3% -1.66% ★ = highlighted strategy used as Signal Congress primary signal. Alpha measured vs. S&P 500 total return over matching 180-day windows, winsorized at ±200%. Past performance does not guarantee future results. HISTORICAL VALIDATION ... ## Research Notes 01 Return windows measured from disclosure date (not transaction date) to reflect real-world signal availability. 02 S&P 500 benchmark uses total return index (dividends reinvested) over identical windows. 03 Win rate = share of trades that outperformed the S&P 500 over the 180-day holding window. 04 Cluster-level returns are trade-weighted, not member-weighted, to avoid concentration bias. 05 Data coverage: 2018–2026. Alpha measurement window: 2023–2026 (180-day lookback constraint). 06 Survivorship bias controlled: all trades including loss-making positions are included. 07 Dollar-range midpoints used for position sizing in weighted return calculations.
